name: Early women’s Kabuki theatre
description: Early Kabuki performers used dance, costume and comic skits; women played both male and female roles.

date.label: mid-to-late 1610s
date.basis: The cited account dates the episode; this is not a claim of global priority.

events.statement: A painting from the mid-to-late 1610s depicts women performing a Kabuki skit.
events.scope: A dated visual witness, not the beginning of Kabuki; later male Kabuki developed different forms.

evidence.supports: The Met dates the screen to the mid-to-late 1610s and identifies female actors playing the roles.
